goal: how do i find contribution info
preamble: It feels like you're hunting for a page somebody buried somewhere on this repository. You're not. Projects that accept outside help almost always keep their rules in a file with a reserved name — CONTRIBUTING.md — and GitHub reads those names and promotes the file into the interface for you. So the task isn't searching. It's knowing which convention to look for, and where GitHub chooses to surface it.
generalization: A handful of filenames are special to GitHub: README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SECURITY. When a repo contains one, GitHub lifts it out of the file list and gives it a permanent place in the sidebar or a banner. So when you want to know a project's rules — how to file a bug, how to behave, how it's licensed — you don't dig through folders. You look for the shortcut the convention already earned.

steps.intent: The right-hand sidebar isn't a menu of links someone typed by hand — it's GitHub reporting which of the standard project files this repo actually has. A Contributing entry there means the maintainers wrote down how they want to be approached: branch rules, commit style, whether they take pull requests at all. Opening it takes you straight to that file, without you needing to know it was called CONTRIBUTING.md or which folder it sat in.
hints: You're after the project's own rules, not its code. GitHub collects that sort of thing — licence, conduct, how to help — in one column away from the file listing.
The sidebar on the right, in the group of links below the About description.
